![](images/47/4727c988042bd8d63af370c507db8988b3024cf7e75c86d40bc70cdcfd744873.png)

Which of the following is equivalent to ${\int }_{C}5\left(y{e}^{x}\right)\,\text{d}x,$ where $C$ is the path along a circle of radius $2,$ traversed from the point $(0,2)$ to the point $(-2,0),$ as shown above?

*Hint: Use the parametrization $r(t)=⟨2\operatorname{cos}⁡t,\,2\operatorname{sin}⁡t⟩.$*
question.:question/worked-solution:
We will use the formula

$$
{\int }_{C}f(x,y)\,\text{d}x={\int }_{a}^{b}f(r(t))\,\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t}\,\text{d}t.
$$

 

The curve $C$ is a part-circle of radius $2$ centered at $O.$ It can be parameterized as 

$$
r(t)=⟨2\operatorname{cos}⁡t,\,2\operatorname{sin}⁡t⟩,\,\frac{\pi }{2}\le t\le \pi .
$$

Computing $\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t},$ we get the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t} & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(2\operatorname{cos}⁡t)=-2\operatorname{sin}⁡t\end{aligned}
$$

Now, since $f(x,y)=5\left(y{e}^{x}\right)$ we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}f(r(t)) & =5\left(2\operatorname{sin}⁡t\cdot {e}^{2\operatorname{cos}⁡t}\right)\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we can write the integral as

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{C}f(x,y)\,\text{d}x & ={\int }_{\pi /2}^{\pi }f(r(t))\,\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t}\,\text{d}t \\  & =5\left({\int }_{\pi /2}^{\pi }2\operatorname{sin}⁡t\cdot {e}^{2\operatorname{cos}⁡t}\cdot (-2\operatorname{sin}⁡t)\,\text{d}t\right)\\  & =5\left(-4{\int }_{\pi /2}^{\pi }{e}^{2\operatorname{cos}⁡t}{sin}^{2}⁡t\,\text{d}t\right)\end{aligned}
$$
